source_reviews.independent_solution: Let H be the perpendicular foot of M on alpha and N the foot on a. For any X in a, MX^2=MH^2+HX^2; minimizing gives d(M,a)^2=MH^2+d(H,a)^2. Thus d(M,alpha)<=d(M,a), with equality exactly when H belongs to a.
With cube edge s>0, distance from a vertex to the opposite face is s. Face diagonal m=s sqrt(2) gives m/sqrt(2); space diagonal d=s sqrt(3) gives d/sqrt(3).

Choose unit normal n and signed distance f(X)=n dot X-t. If midpoint is K, f(K)=(f(A)+f(B))/2. A disjoint segment has endpoints with same sign, so d(K,alpha)=(d(A,alpha)+d(B,alpha))/2. An intersecting segment has opposite signs or a zero endpoint, hence d(K,alpha)=abs(d(A,alpha)-d(B,alpha))/2. A segment contained in the plane gives all zeros. This is a proof via affine signed distance, not an assertion about unsigned distances being affine.

If H is the foot of M, MA^2=MH^2+HA^2 and similarly at B,C; equal spatial distances force H to be the triangle circumcenter. (1) Right triangle circumradius R=sqrt(a^2+b^2)/2, so common distance sqrt(h^2+(a^2+b^2)/4). (2) R=a/(2 sin(alpha)); plane distance sqrt(l^2-a^2/(4 sin(alpha)^2)). Require a,l>0 and 0<alpha<pi, l>=R; equality places M in the plane.

Orthogonal projection of an equidistant spatial point is a planar point equidistant from every vertex. (1) Right triangle: all points on the perpendicular to its plane through the hypotenuse midpoint. (2) Isosceles trapezoid is cyclic, so all points on the perpendicular through its circumcenter. (3) A non-square rhombus is not cyclic: opposite angles are equal and cyclicity would require them supplementary, forcing right angles and a square. Therefore the third locus is empty.

For a line parallel to the plane, signed distance is constant along the line because its direction has zero dot product with a normal. The minimum distance equals the distance from any line point. An intersecting line and plane share a point, so distance is 0.

Set alpha:z=0, A=(0,0,b), B=(a,0,b). AC and BD perpendicular to AB imply C=(0,u,0), D=(a,v,0), where u^2=v^2=C^2-b^2. Write r=sqrt(C^2-b^2). Equal signs give CD=a; opposite signs give CD=sqrt(a^2+4(C^2-b^2)). Both are realizable because no side relation is specified. Genuine obliques require C>b>0; if C=b is allowed they coincide and the obliques degenerate to perpendiculars.

Write parallel planes n dot X=t1 and n dot X=t2 for unit n. Every point in the first has distance abs(t2-t1) from the second, attained along a perpendicular. Intersecting planes share their intersection line, making their distance 0.
For l>0, locus is the two parallel planes n dot X=t+l and t-l. For l=0 it is alpha itself; for l<0 it is empty.

For l>0, d<l is the open slab abs(n dot X-t)<l, including alpha and excluding the two boundary planes. d>l is the union of the two open exterior half-spaces, excluding the boundaries. If l=0 the first is empty and second is all space except alpha; if l<0 the first is empty and second all space.
For distinct parallel planes n dot X=t1,t2, abs(n dot X-t1)=abs(n dot X-t2) implies n dot X=(t1+t2)/2. Only the unique median parallel plane is equidistant, with no exterior component.

Axial symmetry in space is the half-turn about a line p+su. Under the half-turn n becomes 2(u dot n)u-n. To exchange distinct parallel planes requires u dot n=0, and n dot p=(t1+t2)/2. Thus all and only lines contained in the median plane are axes. Their union is that entire plane. An axis perpendicular to the planes leaves their normal coordinate unchanged and cannot exchange them.

(1) Convert 3 dm to 30 cm; put AB=10k, CD=17k. Equal perpendicular components give 100k^2-144=289k^2-900, so k^2=4 and h=sqrt(400-144)=16 cm. (2) If projections p=km, q=kn, then k^2=(a^2-b^2)/(m^2-n^2) and h=sqrt((m^2 b^2-n^2 a^2)/(m^2-n^2)), for m!=n, positive k^2 and positive h^2. If m=n>0, a!=b is impossible; a=b leaves h nonunique (0<h<a for positive projections). (3) For c>0, p+q=c and p^2-q^2=a^2-b^2 give p=(c^2+a^2-b^2)/(2c), q=(c^2-a^2+b^2)/(2c), h=sqrt(((a+b)^2-c^2)*(c^2-(a-b)^2))/(2c). Need p,q>=0 and h>0 for distinct planes; equivalently abs(a^2-b^2)<=c^2<(a+b)^2 (strict lower bound for both projections positive). c=0 is separately possible only if a=b with h=a; these are perpendicular segments.
